Week 14. Pattern: pointer manipulation.

Reverse a singly linked list in place and return the new head. O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

Complete the class ReverseList in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public static Node reverse(Node head)

The Node class is provided; don't include it in your answer.

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.

generalfeedback.text: Pattern: pointer manipulation. Compare your answer with the reference solution in practice/dsa/solutions, then write one line in your NOTES.md: the pattern, the complexity, and the mistake you made.

Week 16. Pattern: recursion with bounds.

Return whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree: every value in a node's left subtree is strictly smaller and every value in its right subtree strictly larger. Checking only the children is not enough.

The TreeNode class is provided; don't include it in your answer.

Week 19. Pattern: topological sort (Kahn's algorithm).

End-of-day batch jobs depend on each other: dependsOn.get("interest") lists jobs that must finish before "interest". Every job appears as a key. Return an order that runs each job after its dependencies, choosing the alphabetically smallest ready job whenever several are ready, or empty if there is a cycle.

Complete the class JobOrder in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public static Optional<List<String>> order(Map<String, List<String>> dependsOn)

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.

generalfeedback.text: Pattern: topological sort (Kahn's algorithm). Compare your answer with the reference solution in practice/dsa/solutions, then write one line in your NOTES.md: the pattern, the complexity, and the mistake you made.

testcode.text: System.out.println(JobOrder.order(Map.of( "close-day", List.of("interest", "fees"), "interest", List.of("load-balances"), "fees", List.of("load-balances"), "load-balances", List.<String>of(), "audit", List.<String>of())));

Week 22. Pattern: hash map plus access order.

A name-enquiry cache holding at most capacity entries. get and put are O(1); when full, put of a new key evicts the least recently used entry (a get or put counts as a use). You may use LinkedHashMap or build your own list + map; be ready to explain both in an interview.

Complete the class LruCache in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public LruCache(int capacity)
  • public Optional<V> get(K key)
  • public void put(K key, V value)
  • public int size()

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.
